report.source_text: A computed tomography (CT) scan of her abdomen/pelvis identified a right groin lesion measuring 6.4 × 4.9 × 6.3 cm, and a retroperitoneal mass (11.5 × 10.6 × 17.4 cm) causing right-sided hydronephrosis (see Fig. 1a). Furthermore, an extensive deep vein thrombosis (DVT) involved the common iliac and femoral vessels. Lastly, there were pathologically enlarged lymph nodes in the celiac axis, retrocrural space, and external iliac chains. A CT scan of her thorax revealed left-side neck adenopathy measuring 3 × 3 cm but no parenchymal lung lesions were noted.

clinician.final_diagnosis: a stage IIIC germ cell tumor
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 38-year-old transgender female on hormone therapy presented with right-sided scrotal swelling, abdominal and back pain, fatigue, and weight loss. Imaging (CT) revealed a large right groin lesion and extensive retroperitoneal masses with nodal involvement causing hydronephrosis, as well as extensive DVT and cervical adenopathy (E001). Initial tumor markers showed markedly elevated LDH and β-HCG, and normal AFP, consistent with germ cell tumor (E002). A right radical inguinal orchiectomy pathology demonstrated no malignancy but scarring from treatment effect (E006). The patient received BEP chemotherapy with discontinuation of hormonal therapy (E004), resulting in normalization of tumor markers post-treatment (E005) and reduction of the retroperitoneal mass on restaging CT (E007). Histopathological confirmation from the orchiectomy was lacking due to treatment effect and no biopsy from other masses was reported. Physical examination details at presentation were not documented. The clinical, radiological, biochemical, and treatment response findings support a diagnosis of stage IIIC germ cell tumor.
